title: PAS lets designated actors operate rate limits and pre-approved actions without administrative control over the PAU
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4 defines the PAS (Parallelized Allocation System) as "a permissioned layer that lets designated actors operate a Diamond PAU's rate limits and pre-approved controller actions, within governance-set ceilings, without direct administrative control over the Diamond PAU."

The last clause is the design claim. Rate limits are themselves a privileged control — the Controller Role can "update the Rate Limits contract" per A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.2.2 — so delegating their day-to-day operation would normally mean handing over the ability to relax them. PAS resolves this by making delegation ceiling-bounded: an actor may move a limit within a range governance has already approved, and cannot reach past it or reconfigure the Instance.

Two contracts implement the split. The Configurator (A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.3.6) is the entry point through which those actors operate limits and pre-approved actions, and BeamState (A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.3.7) "records which actors, rate limits, and controller actions are authorized." Authorization is therefore explicit on-chain state rather than an implication of holding a role.

All three sections close with "Further details will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas" — the boundary is committed to while the mechanics remain open, which is worth tracking as a known gap rather than reading as a complete specification.
description: The Parallelized Allocation System is a permissioned layer bounded by governance-set ceilings, with BeamState recording which actors, limits and actions are authorized;
